verses.1: And now, listen, Jacob, my servant! I have chosen Israel for this purpose.
verses.2: Thus said Jehovah: “I have created you from nothing. I will help you. Do not be afraid, my servant Jacob! I have chosen him as your leader.”
verses.3: For waters will flow over your land, and floods will cover your crops. The Spirit of God will be upon your descendants, and I will bless your offspring.
verses.4: And they grew among the bushes, like weeds on the banks of the rivers.
verses.5: This will say to Jehovah, “I.” This will be called by the name of Jacob. This will write down Jehovah’s name with its own hand. And in the name of Israel, it will be written down.
verses.6: As Jehovah, king of Israel, says: “The Lord, with His armies, will save us. I am the first and I will also be the last. And without me, there is no God.”
verses.7: And from my heart, it will be called out, and it will speak to me. It will arrange everything for me from my depths, with nations and ages. And those who come will tell me what to do.
verses.8: Do not be afraid, and do not despair. Since you heard and learned from me, and you are witnesses that there is a God besides me; no creature can be known without my knowledge.
verses.9: All those who create things are foolish; their works are worthless. They do not know what they are doing, and they do nothing useful.
verses.10: Who created heaven and earth? He set them in place, so that they wouldn’t be destroyed.
verses.11: And all their friends will also be destroyed. All those who are like humans will be defeated. They will stand in fear, and they will all be destroyed together.
verses.12: He forged iron into tools and used it in various applications. He also worked with charcoal and other materials to create his creations. His strength was so great that he could even work without drinking water at all.
verses.13: The carved wood will be shaped and decorated in the right manner. It will be crafted as a beautiful piece of art, just like how a man decorates his home with beautiful decorations.
verses.14: He planted trees for him. He took saplings and iron, and he planted them in the trees of the forest. He also planted wheat and barley.
verses.15: And it would be for man to make bread from them. He would take some of them, bake them, and then eat them. But he wouldn’t use any yeast or anything like that. Instead, he would just bake them without using any additives. Then he would worship those breads as gods.
verses.16: Half of it was burned by fire. On half of it, birds ate the flesh. It became covered with ashes. Even the bones were destroyed. And they said, “Oh, my heat! I have seen light.”
verses.17: And those who remain will worship Him, bow down before Him, and pray to Him. They will say, “Save me, for You are my God.”
verses.18: They will not know or understand that it is true from the sight of their eyes, from what is clear to their minds.
verses.19: And he will not return to his heart, nor will he understand. There will be no solution; I have burned half of it with fire, and I’ve also made it into bread for eating. But it will still be a source of suffering. I will make it into a tree that causes harm.
verses.20: He will be cast into the abyss, where he will not be able to save his soul. Nor will he be able to say, “Alas, what a lie I have said in my own time.”
verses.21: Remember these: Jacob and Israel. For You created them as Your servants. You made them Your people, Israel. Do not abandon me.
verses.22: I have punished you for your sins, and I have made your wickedness return to you, because I have saved you.
verses.23: May the heavens rejoice, for Jehovah has done great things! The mountains have been made to tremble, and all trees in them have flourished. For Jehovah has redeemed Jacob, and Israel will be honored.
verses.24: As the LORD has said, “Behold, I will make you great and create you from nothing. I, the LORD, do all things alone. The earth lies hidden from me.”
verses.25: May his words be praised in days to come. May the wise men rejoice, and their wisdom be preserved forever.
verses.26: May their works be done, and may the plans of their craftsmen be fulfilled. May Jerusalem be rebuilt, and may its ruins be restored.
verses.27: The words of destruction and ruin are spoken against you, O Oviš.
verses.28: Let Korash Roi and all my desires be satisfied. And let it be said in Jerusalem: “It will be built, and its halls will be used.”
